summary: The design has broad forward coverage and generally fits the real query/view/TUI architecture, with no material scope creep found. Approval is blocked by an unhandled, ordinary record -a archive boundary across pgcenter upgrades and by acceptance proofs that do not discriminate several load-bearing SQL contracts. This was a static source/artifact review; no live PG 19 stand or mutation run was executed.

designOrTasks: Explicit column layout in Data Models
Decision 3 specifies ORDER BY s.score DESC
No discriminating rounded-tie fixture or explicit automated assertion is scheduled
Data Models specifies n_dead_tup and a LEFT JOIN on relid
The listed tests do not pin the join type/key or missing-partner behavior
The listed tests do not distinguish it from the joined-side schema
SC-1 and SC-8 require growing values
Expected values are only described as consistent with reset, without a direct DB-to-report comparison or timing tolerance
SC-8 explicitly requires untouched relations to remain blank
Fresh disposable PG 19 container and pg19_stats_age_report_unavailable base checkpoint
Final DB-to-report expected-value evidence and timing tolerance are not specified
Regression base and final replay assertions

findings.issue: The record -a pgcenter-upgrade path is not benign end to end. Decision 1 and the Risks table prove only that diff() remains in bounds when two PG 19 samples have different widths. report.formatStatSample returns early whenever view.Aligned is true, and only a recorded server-version change clears that state. A narrow pre-feature PG 19 archive appended by the feature binary therefore reuses the old 19/6-entry ColsWidth map for a 20/7-column result. With populated stats_age, printStatSample returns 'zero or negative width, skip'; with NULL stats_age it can instead retain the old header/layout. This contradicts the 'benign mismatch', 'Recorded archives: unaffected', and 'Breaking changes: no' claims.
findings.location: Tech spec Decision 1, Testing Strategy bounds invariant, Backward Compatibility, and final Risks row; report/report.go:276-320 and 527-538, 616-640; record/recorder.go:64-99
findings.fix: Handle a result-layout change as a replay boundary, not only a server-version change: compare the incoming and previous column layouts, drop the previous snapshot, and reset Aligned/Cols/ColsWidth, header cadence, and requested-sort state exactly as the version-change branch does. Add same-190000 narrow-to-wide tables and indexes fixtures with at least two ticks per pgcenter layout, populated stats_age, and a requested sort column. If mixed pgcenter-layout archives are deliberately unsupported instead, remove the benign/unaffected claims and add an explicit validation error plus release-note workaround; do not leave the current silent/erroring behavior undocumented.

findings.issue: Several core SQL and stats_age checks have contracts but no discriminating evidence plan. The new-query unit test is specified to pin names/order and only the outer FROM relation; it does not pin ORDER BY s.score, the LEFT JOIN and relid key, or outer-side s.schemaname. An implementation using the rounded ORDER BY alias, an INNER JOIN, or joined-side schemaname could satisfy all listed automated checks. SC-5's generic representative relations do not guarantee the three raw scores that collapse to 0.00, and an unmatched join partner cannot be relied on in a live catalog. SC-1 likewise says only 'consistent with the reset', without naming DB evidence, active/untouched relation selection, or an elapsed-time tolerance.
findings.location: Tech spec Test Data and Identifier Map rows Score values/dead_total/Acceptance reset, Unit tests, Integration tests, Acceptance Design SC-1 and SC-5; user spec AC-7-AC-9 and AC-27
findings.fix: Extend the query structure test with explicit assertions for all six round expressions, boolean casts, outer relation concatenation, LEFT JOIN pg_stat_all_tables on relid, outer s.schemaname in the predicate, and qualified unrounded ORDER BY. Port the already measured three-relation rounded-tie fixture into an integration assertion whose expected row order distinguishes raw-score sorting, and use structural evidence for the unmatched LEFT JOIN case. For SC-1/SC-8, capture direct DB stats_reset evidence for chosen active and untouched tables/indexes and compare public report/TUI values with a stated seconds/tick tolerance. Keep the existing feature-missing base checkpoints.

findings.issue: The unit-test plan requires asserting the refusal's composed cmdline line while also acknowledging that printCmdline is unobservable. The proposed architecture leaves the write inside menuSelect and introduces no decision/message seam. Testing composeCmdline with a literal notice would not prove that menuSelect selected that notice or avoided a second write.
findings.location: Tech spec Unit tests final bullet and Decision 7; top/menu.go:149-250; top/ui.go printCmdline/composeCmdline path
findings.fix: Either extract a pure tables-menu selection result used by menuSelect (target, whether to switch, and exact message), so the branch and one-write construction are testable, or remove the claimed composed-line unit assertion and retain exact-message/exactly-once verification as code review plus manual SC-7.

findings.issue: Registering the first production NotRecordable view creates a misleading PG 19 record message. filterViews increments one shared filtered counter for both NotRecordable and version failures; on PG 19 with pg_stat_statements present, autovacuum_scores can be the only dropped view, causing setup to print that statistics are unsupported by the current PostgreSQL version even though the screen is supported and deliberately excluded from recording.
findings.location: Tech spec NotRecordable/AC-31 design; record/record.go:83-89 and 199-232
findings.fix: Separate unsupported-version and deliberately-not-recordable skip reasons, or reword the aggregate INFO so it covers both. Add a PG 19 filter/setup test that proves the new view is absent without claiming it is unsupported.
